items.title: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow, targets $70–$78/share on Nasdaq
items.summary: Anthropic kicked off the investor roadshow for its IPO on November 10, with an expected price range of $70.00–$78.00 per share. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker "ANT", following its confidential S-1 filing earlier this year.
items.whyItMatters: A successful IPO brings fresh capital and scrutiny to Anthropic's roadmap — the LLM brain behind tutor feedback and lesson generation — though no API pricing or product changes land today.

items.title: Nvidia board formalizes independent probe into Huang's China-linked affair
items.summary: Nvidia's board has assembled a committee of independent directors with outside counsel to investigate CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a Megaspeed executive US intelligence reportedly believed was passing information to China. Huang admitted the affair and says he'll cooperate fully; the board says it has no reason to believe trade secrets were compromised, and he remains in charge. Separately, members of Congress set a November 11 deadline for Huang to accept a closed-door briefing.
items.whyItMatters: Nvidia GPUs sit underneath nearly every voice/LLM vendor the tutor depends on, so sustained leadership turmoil — even without a product impact yet — is worth tracking for supply and pricing risk.

items.title: Stanford's AI100 report: the scaling era may be plateauing
items.summary: The third report in Stanford's 100-Year Study on AI, "AI Goes Mainstream: The Scaling Era and the Rise of Generative AI," argues that pure scaling is running short of new high-quality training data and that compute costs for frontier models are becoming prohibitive.
items.whyItMatters: If brute-force scaling is genuinely hitting diminishing returns, the next gains for a voice tutor's LLM brain are more likely to come from better data, distillation and architecture than from ever-bigger models — worth watching for where to invest build effort.
